body.translated_text: Oṃ. Homage to the glorious blessed <s>Vajravārāhī</s>.

children.translated_text: Having arisen from the ornament of the ocean of bliss, that splendor of the fully awakened one,
endowed with all forms of virtue, she who destroys the mass of darkness of the world's sins,
the radiance of the treasure of the light of <s>jñāna</s> (wisdom), the peace of the treasure of <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness), [the glory] of the treasure of <s>manīṣā</s> (insight) —
may the blessed <s>Vajravirāsinī</s> protect the three worlds from misfortune. // Tjs 0.1 //

children.text: śrīvajradevīpadapadmareṇu, rājiṃ namaskṛtya guroḥ padaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Having bowed to the line of pollen-dust from the lotus-feet of the glorious <s>Vajradevī</s>, and to the feet of the <s>Guru</s>,
[and to] the glorious <s>Saṃbara</s>, the concealed <s>bodhicitta</s> (awakening-mind), the praised state of non-duality of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>kṛpā</s> (compassion) — // Tjs 0.2 //
By the monk <s>Jñānandra</s>, who abides in the bliss of worshipping the pair of feet of <s>Vajradevī</s>,
[who is also known as] <s>Candrevasuvaśarman</s> — // Tjs 0.3 //
The <s>sādhana</s> (practice) of <s>Vajravārāhī</s> is expounded somewhat for one's own benefit.
In [this work] which always bestows well-spoken [teachings], the mind is eagerly inclined toward composition. // Tjs 0.4 //
Therefore, by me who is devoted to faith, of dull and limited intellect,

children.text: karttavya na mama doṣo vīkṣaṇīyo mahājanaiḥ // Tjs_0.5 //
children.translated_text: this is to be done — my faults should not be examined by the great ones. // Tjs 0.5 //
Arisen from the sole-<s>cakra</s> (wheel), stirred by the wind, blazing like a flash of lightning,
having burned the three <s>āli</s>s (vowel-rows), honored by the three worlds, bathed in a stream of nectar,
turbid with the juice of Buddha-<s>jñāna</s> (wisdom), free from defilement, bestowing a flood of self-bliss,
devoid of deliberation on existence and non-existence — may the <s>Vārāhī</s> protect you! // Tjs 1.1 //
blazing with the fire of <s>prajñā</s>-<s>āla</s>, with a flow of nectar, like the thread of a subtle primordial cord,
she who burns the cluster of <s>vidyā</s>-Buddhas, who pierces the three <s>cakras</s> (wheels) —

children.text: sānandā lalitordvagā sphuratu vo vārāhikā cetasi // Tjs_1.2 //
children.translated_text: may the blissful, gracefully ascending <s>Vārāhī</s> flash forth in your mind! // Tjs 1.2 //

body.translated_text: Situated in the sun-disk of the <s>nirmāṇa-āli</s> (emanation vowel-row), enveloped by the letters beginning with <s>ka</s>,

children.translated_text: Having prostrated to <s>Vārāhī</s>, preceded by '<s>vajra</s>,' the <s>Vajrayoginī</s>,

children.text: śirasā svasmṛtaye vakṣye 'haṃ tattvajñānasya saṃsiddhim // Tjs_1.3 //
children.translated_text: with [bowed] head, for my own recollection, I shall expound the accomplishment of <s>tattvajñāna</s> (reality-knowledge). // Tjs 1.3 //
The wise one, [bearing] the lord's mark, should enter a secluded place agreeable to the mind.
There, having sat upon a comfortable seat, one should contemplate purification. // Tjs 1.4 //
Then, with the heart[-mantra] of <s>Vajradhara</s>, recited with three syllables by the sixth <s>Jina</s> (Buddha),
one should inscribe [it] with the ring finger and make an offering of red flowers. // Tjs 1.5 //
Then, in the supreme first vessel, placing the left lotus-hand,
one should perform the oblation (<s>savana</s>) as instructed, through the touch of repose. // Tjs 1.6 //
Having performed the hand-<s>nyāsa</s> (placement), through the joining of the thumb and [ring] finger,
one should perform the body-<s>nyāsa</s> (placement) with the six <s>Vīreśvarī</s> <s>mantras</s>. // Tjs 1.7 //
Then, upon the <s>cakra-vajra</s> (wheel-thunderbolt) platform, [one should place] the <s>mantra</s> equal to the stage-red union,
and scatter nail-clippings in the interstices, distinguished by serpent-born [substances]. // Tjs 1.8 //
There, having inscribed the <s>Jina</s>-heart-<s>cakra</s> (Buddha-heart-wheel) with a flame-tip,
one should write the <s>mantra</s>-garland within its center with a stylus of gold. // Tjs 1.9 //
On the outer part of the <s>cakra</s>, in the directions of east, north, west, and south,
one should inscribe <s>svastika</s>s in sequence with the left hand. // Tjs 1.10 //
Having attracted <s>Vajradevī</s>, having [her] enter into the <s>mantra</s>-syllables, having bound [her], one should please [her].

children.text: suvidhānāt jaḥ huṃ vaṃ horiti paṭhitvā // Tjs_1.11 //
children.translated_text: Through proper ritual, having recited '<s>jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ</s>' — // Tjs 1.11 //
Then one should perform various worship (<s>saparyā</s>) of her who has the form of <s>mantra</s>,
with eatables, foods, lickables, drinkables, and suckables, endowed with desirable qualities, // Tjs 1.12 //
with various offerings (<s>bali</s>), pleasing gifts, five exceedingly precious <s>upahāras</s> (presentations),
with songs, instrumental music, dances, circumambulations, prostrations, and praises. // Tjs 1.13 //

children.text: pratidivasaṃ pratipakṣaṃ pratimāsaṃ vā tithau daśamyāṃ /
children.translated_text: Every day, every fortnight, or every month, on the tenth <s>tithi</s> (lunar day),
one who desires <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment) should perform the worship-rite of her as prescribed. // Tjs 1.14 //

body.translated_text: Then, having completed the external worship rite, [the practitioner] of great compassion, in the <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) on the destruction of enemies,
should meditate upon the previously described <s>Devī</s> as a hot, life-bereft image. // Tjs 2.1 //

children.translated_text: Of the color of twilight-vermilion, with the brilliance of seven suns setting upon the edge of a donkey-[headed] ray-cluster,
the doer [of all], the remover of all afflictions, bearing radiant nectar-compassion in her right arm,
holding in her left arm an exceedingly white lotus, resplendent with a banner filled with red [blood],
whose head is surrounded by <s>Kālī</s>, thunderbolt-<s>Kālī</s>, with hand raised in liberation above the head — // Tjs 2.2 //
her body adorned with a garland of skulls, blood flowing from [her] mouth and throat, emitting a pleasing sound of roaring,
On the left, with an upward-turned face, with beautiful and auspicious gait, with wrathful expression at the root and extremity of the face,
filled with bliss, filled with passion, endowed with various <s>rasas</s> (sentiments), dancing in <s>ardhaparyaṅka</s> (half-seated posture),
with limbs sealed by six <s>mudrās</s>, without garments, sixteen years of age, with beautiful limbs.
Having performed the procedure of <s>jñānākarṣa</s> (wisdom-attraction) and so forth as before, the knowledgeable ritualist (<s>mantrī</s>),
should meditate on a single <s>svastika</s>-garland revolving rapidly, facing forward.
Then, in the space-like element, in the cave of the three-peaked mountain (<s>Trikūṭagiri</s>), the revolving <s>cakra</s> (wheel),
should be meditated upon as described before, red and blazing brightly.
There, as if steady despite great speed, shining like an unwavering lamp in a windless place,
one should cause the great-bliss <s>cakra</s> to flow, performing the oblation made of the essence of dripping <s>amṛta</s> (nectar).
Having the nature of the three bodies (<s>kāyatraya</s>), supreme, innately self-natured (<s>sahajātmaka</s>), pervading the universe,
manifesting a limitless peaceful continuum — one should see bliss thereafter, and again thereafter.
One should contemplate this every day, at every twilight junction (<s>sandhyā</s>), or at every moment,
until the signs of accomplishment (<s>siddhi</s>) appear; this is said to be clearly [established].

body.translated_text: When this contemplation becomes clearly manifest through the connection of effortlessly-born bliss and absorption (<s>laya</s>),

body.text: kaśācapeṭādiha naiva vedanā tadā bhavetsiddhiradūravarttinī // Tjs_2.8 //
body.translated_text: and there is no sensation from whipping, slapping, and so forth, then accomplishment (<s>siddhi</s>) is not far away.

children.translated_text: If the loud sound of struck drums (<s>paṇava</s>) and other instruments becomes imperceptible to hearing,
when unsurpassed supreme awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) is attained — in dreams, after long practice, the foremost accomplishment of the meditator [appears].
Having seen the signs of accomplishment (<s>siddhi</s>), in ancestral groves, mountain bowers, at the foot of trees, and so forth,
the wise one, dwelling there, should continuously practice <s>utpannakramayoga</s> (completion stage yoga).
In accomplishment, the dissolution of earth (<s>vasudhā</s>) and the other [elements] occurs progressively in succession,

children.text: khyāti tadā gaganābhaṃ prabhāsvaraṃ jñānamātraṃ sat // Tjs_2.11 //
children.translated_text: then there shines forth what is sky-like, luminous (<s>prabhāsvara</s>), being pure knowledge alone.
One should know it by its signs; the knowledgeable ones know the signs to be fivefold,

children.text: ata eva tāni yogī samāhito lakṣayenmanasā // Tjs_2.12 //
children.translated_text: therefore the <s>yogī</s>, absorbed in concentration, should observe them with the mind.
The first [sign] is like a mirage (<s>mṛgatṛṣṇā</s>); the second sign is smoke-like,
the third is like a firefly (<s>khadyota</s>); the fourth is clearly like a blazing lamp,
the fifth sign is like a cloudless sky, luminous and free of conceptual elaboration (<s>avikalpa</s>);
thus, having obtained the signs, one attains the great <s>mudrā</s> (seal).

children.text: utthātukāmaḥ praṇipatya yoginīṃ nāthaṃ ca kasthaṃ samudīrya mūḥ kṛtiṃ /
children.translated_text: Wishing to arise, having prostrated to the <s>yoginī</s> and the lord (<s>nātha</s>), having uttered the syllable at the throat, performing the ritual action,

children.text: utthāya kṛtyaṃ vidadhīta tatvadhīstiṣṭhetsadā yogayugena yogavit // Tjs_2.15 //
children.translated_text: having risen, one should perform the [daily] activities; the knower of truth should always remain yoked in yoga, being a knower of yoga.

body.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Tattvajñānasaṃsiddhi</s>, [ends] the method of meditation (<s>bhāvanāvidhi</s>). Chapter 2.
And having been entreated many times by disciples who have prepared the <s>maṇḍala</s> and bowed at the lotus feet,
the ritualist (<s>mantrī</s>), on the tenth lunar day (<s>tithi</s>), should perform their consecration (<s>anugraha</s>).

children.translated_text: Having worshipped the goddess (<s>devī</s>) in the form of the <s>mantra</s>, established in the <s>cakra</s>, having performed the ritual sequence,
taking up the foremost <s>mantra</s> that has been recited, one should proceed from that [place].
Then, having prepared the five <s>maṇḍalas</s>, [with the deity] established on the head, and then [positioning] the disciple to the south,

children.text: kusumasrajaṃ dadhānaṃ dhyātakenāthaṃ guruḥ paśyet // Tjs_3.3a //
children.translated_text: bearing a garland of flowers, the <s>guru</s> should visualize the lord (<s>nātha</s>) through meditation.

children.text: tadanu ca yathoktaṃ devīcakraṃ prodyanmarīcikaṃ rayavat /
children.translated_text: Then, as described, the <s>devī</s>'s <s>cakra</s>, rising with rays of light, radiant,
having meditated [on it] within the body of the initiate, the <s>vajra</s>-holder should transmit it.
Thus there would be possession (<s>āveśa</s>): the budding [experience], trembling, tears,
falling, the arising of knowledge (<s>jñānotpāda</s>), and the realization of one's own nature — these are to be brought about.
Thereafter, one should teach the <s>samādhi</s>, worship (<s>pūjā</s>), and <s>mantra</s> of <s>Vajrayoginī</s>,
to one who is endowed with faith, possessed of virtues, and has genuine devotion seeing the <s>guru</s> as inseparable from the <s>Buddha</s>.

body.translated_text: One should not teach this yoga — even if immediately convincing or well-accomplished —
to a disciple whose mind is devoid of faith and who lacks devotion.

children.translated_text: But whoever performs worship of the <s>devī</s>'s <s>cakra</s> joined with <s>mantra</s>,

children.text: tasyāpayānti bhayānyaṣṭau pāpāni ca mahānti // Tjs_3.8 //
children.translated_text: from that person the eight fears and great sins depart.
Misfortune, poverty, disease, old age, suffering, and despondency,
delusion, strife, defilement, afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>), and various kinds of torment —

children.text: yo japati cakramantraṃ dhyātvā hṛdaye nirodhavācāsau /
children.translated_text: whoever recites the <s>cakra</s> <s>mantra</s>, having meditated in the heart with restrained speech,
attains the eight <s>siddhis</s> (accomplishments), the five <s>abhijñās</s> (supernatural knowledges), and likewise the eight qualities.

body.text: dhyāyati yaḥ kiravaktrāṃ pratidavasaṃ yatnataścatuḥsaṃdhyaṃ hariharahiraṇyagarbhairjetumaśakyāṃ mṛtiṃ jayati // Tjs_3.11 //
body.translated_text: He who meditates upon the ray-faced one diligently at the four <s>saṃdhyās</s> (junctures of the day) every day, conquers death which is unconquerable even by <s>Hari</s>, <s>Hara</s>, and <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>. // Tjs_3.11 //

children.translated_text: Garments, food, drink, wealth, grain, vast lands, palaces, divine beds, seats, and implements —

children.text: tasyodbhavanti dayitā vividhāśca vidyā, yo bhāvayatyaśanikolamukhīṃ sacakrāṃ // 12 //
children.translated_text: all these arise for him, along with beloved ones and manifold knowledge, who contemplates the thunderbolt-mouthed one (<s>Aśanikolamukhī</s>) with her <s>cakra</s> (wheel). // 12 //

body.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Tattvajñānasaṃsiddhi</s>, [ends] the procedure for the blessing of disciples, together with its rewards.

children.translated_text: I shall now teach the supreme <s>mantra-uddhāra</s> (mantra extraction), the heart of <s>Vajrayoginī</s>,
which has come from ear to ear, from mouth to mouth, in proper succession. // Tjs_4.1 //
One should draw a <s>cakra</s> (diagram) as previously described, furnished with the abode of the <s>Marudgaṇas</s> (wind-gods),

children.text: tatra likhetparipāṭita ālikāliṃ tathaiva koṇaṃ // Tjs_4.2 //
children.translated_text: and therein one should inscribe in order the <s>āli-kāli</s> (vowel and consonant series), and likewise the corners. // Tjs_4.2 //
Having <s>jha</s> below, <s>ḍa</s> placed beneath, adorned with <s>ha</s> below, joined together,
the group of three should be written first, with the syllable, illuminating the <s>tattva</s> (reality). // Tjs_4.3 //
<s>Bha</s> placed above, joined with <s>cha</s> above, <s>ṭa</s> placed above — these should then be written,
joined with <s>ḍa</s> below, having <s>ṣa</s> as base, joined with <s>ṣa</s> above and <s>śa</s> above. // Tjs_4.4 //
Joined with <s>ña</s> below, <s>ḷa</s> placed at the bottom, joined with <s>ṭa</s> below and <s>pa</s> placed above,
then <s>ṭha</s> below joined with <s>pha</s> above, combined with <s>ai</s> and <s>vā</s>, <s>ha</s> and <s>ṭa</s> placed within. // Tjs_4.5 //
<s>Ca</s> placed in the middle, joined with <s>ṭha</s> on the left, <s>bha</s> below and <s>su</s> well-placed,

children.text: tadanu hathamadhyagataṃ tavāmayuktaṃ ṭhalamadhyaga paścāt // Tjs_4.6 //
children.translated_text: then <s>ha</s> and <s>tha</s> in the middle, joined with <s>ta</s> on the left, <s>ṭha</s>, <s>la</s> in the middle afterwards. // Tjs_4.6 //
<s>Pha</s> in the middle at the end of all actions, joined with the first of the third group (<s>varga</s>) on the left,

children.text: ṇorddhayutaṃ lādharagaṃ chorddhasthaṃ bhatalagaṃ ṭhasavyayutaṃ // Tjs_4.7 //
children.translated_text: joined with <s>ṇa</s> above, <s>la</s> below, <s>cha</s> above, <s>bha</s> and <s>ta</s> at the bottom, joined with <s>ṭha</s> on the left. // Tjs_4.7 //
Joined with <s>ta</s> above, <s>ṣa</s> below, joined with <s>tha</s> above and <s>da</s>, <s>ṇa</s> below afterwards,

children.text: phādharagaṃ ṭhādharasaṃyuktaṃ phorddhasthaṃ ṇorddhayuktaṃ lādharagaṃ // Tjs_4.8 //
children.translated_text: <s>Pha</s> below, joined with <s>ṭha</s> below, <s>pha</s> above, joined with <s>ṇa</s> above, <s>la</s> below. // Tjs_4.8 //
Joined with <s>ḍa</s> below and <s>śūnya</s> (zero/void), <s>tri</s> and <s>va</s> at the bottom, <s>ca</s> above, <s>ra</s> at the bottom,
joined with <s>tha</s> below, <s>śa</s> as base, joined with <s>ña</s> below as well. // Tjs_4.9 //
<s>Sa</s> and <s>ya</s> in the middle, joined with <s>jha</s> on the left — this secret is composed of the aforementioned syllables.
This <s>mantra</s> of the goddess <s>Aśanī</s> (Vajrayoginī) should be written, recited, and meditated upon. // Tjs_4.10 //

The wish-fulfilling gem (<s>Cintāmaṇi</s>), the tip of the wish-granting tree (<s>Kalpataru</s>), the <s>Kumbha</s> (vessel of plenty), and the glorious wish-fulfilling cow (<s>Kāmadhenu</s>) are praised,

children.text: te sādhyamānā dadatīha vittānyayantu saukhyaṃ sadhanaṃ dadāti // Tjs_4.11 //
children.translated_text: but when propitiated, they bestow only material wealth; this, however, bestows happiness together with wealth. // Tjs_4.11 //

body.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Tattvajñānasaṃsiddhi</s>, [ends] the procedure for <s>mantra</s> extraction.

children.translated_text: The knower of proper rites should inscribe this upon a vessel for the purpose of worship,
and the protection of a child should be duly performed, by binding [the amulet] on the arm, throat, topknot, or upper arm of the elder. // 1 //

children.text: dṛṣṭvāpayānti bhujagāḥ śiśukaṃ sarakṣaṃ, bhūtā grahā niśicarāḥ sapiśācasaṃghāḥ /
children.translated_text: Seeing the child with this protection, serpents flee, as do <s>bhūtas</s> (spirits), <s>grahas</s> (seizing demons), night-wanderers (<s>niśicaras</s>), and hosts of <s>piśācas</s>,

children.text: anye ca bālakabharyārttikarāḥ subhīmāḥ siṃhaṃ yathā vanacarā valinambhayārttāḥ // 2 //
children.translated_text: and other terrifying beings who cause suffering to children — just as forest-dwelling animals flee in terror from a lion. // 2 //

children.text: saṃprāpya sadupadeśaṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃpratyayaṃ ca yogasya /
children.translated_text: Having received the excellent teaching and having seen the proof of <s>yoga</s>,
this <s>siddhi</s> (attainment) was written down, a lineage of radiant, pure knowledge. // 3 //
Therefore, for the attainment of that, one should serve the lotus feet of the <s>guru</s>,
through the rite of offering gifts, through bodily austerities, and through prostrations. // 4 //
The supreme attainment of <s>tattvajñāna</s> (knowledge of reality), which produces great benefit for people in the world,
by which beings become wholesome and stainless, radiant as the rays of the former moon —
may the worlds, freed from the impurity of the <s>Kali</s> (age of darkness), become recipients of pure awakening (<s>śuddha-sambodhi</s>) through that,
having obtained the noble <s>mudrā</s> (seal) that pacifies the fear of worldly existence and accomplishes the welfare of all beings. // 5 //

body.translated_text: Here ends the <s>Tattvajñānasaṃsiddhi</s>, named the self-empowerment (<s>svādhiṣṭhāna</s>). May there be auspiciousness always.
